title: Gender parity is improving slowly while leadership, political power, AI roles, and financial-market representation remain sharply unequal
source_unit: World Economic Forum, Global Gender Gap Report 2026
geography: 145 economies in the 2026 index, with a constant comparison set of 143 economies between 2025 and 2026 and deeper labor, political, AI, leadership, and financial-market analysis

denominator.unit: economies included in the 2026 Global Gender Gap Index

overall_parity.unit: percent of the global gender gap closed in the 2026 index

constant_sample_change.unit: percentage-point improvement among 143 economies covered in both 2025 and 2026

long_run_change.unit: percentage-point improvement from the 2006 global score for the comparable long-run set

observations.method: World Economic Forum Global Gender Gap Index benchmarking economic participation, education, health, and political empowerment using latest available international data.
observations.uncertainty: Index scores summarize different indicators and data vintages; missing economies, measurement changes, weighting, and cross-country comparability affect interpretation. A closed gap is not an absolute welfare or rights measure.
observations.subgroup: Women and men across economies, regions, income groups, economic participation, education, health, and political empowerment dimensions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Small aggregate movement can conceal meaningful country-level progress or reversal; parity scores do not show whether gains are durable, equally distributed, or experienced as agency.

observations.period: 2026; economic participation and political empowerment gaps

denominator.unit: economies included in the 2026 subindex comparison

economic_participation_parity.unit: percent of the economic-participation and opportunity gap closed

political_empowerment_parity.unit: percent of the political-empowerment gap closed

professional_technical_parity.unit: percent parity score for professional and technical workers

senior_leadership_parity.unit: percent parity score for legislators, senior officials, and managers

observations.method: WEF subindex analysis of labor-market participation, occupational representation, leadership, and political empowerment.
observations.uncertainty: Parity scores compare representation or outcomes between women and men but do not measure job quality, authority, discrimination mechanisms, unpaid work, or intersectional differences.
observations.subgroup: Women and men in professional and technical occupations, management, senior public roles, legislatures, and political leadership.
observations.counterinterpretation: Representation gains can broaden role models and decision-making access even before parity is reached; low parity in leadership does not imply no progress in other labor-market dimensions.

denominator.unit: economies with data used to compare women’s representation from entry-level positions to the C-suite

entry_to_c_suite.value: women’s representation drops from 46.0 percent at entry level to 23.0 percent at the C-suite

pipeline_loss.unit: percentage-point decline in women’s representation from entry level to C-suite

long_run_leadership.value: women hold 3 percent more top jobs than ten years ago

observations.method: WEF analysis of leadership-pipeline data and corporate representation across 57 economies.
observations.uncertainty: The pipeline comparison is not a causal decomposition of promotion, retention, occupation, sector, or selection processes; firms and economies differ in coverage and role definitions.
observations.subgroup: Women and men at entry, management, senior leadership, and C-suite levels across sectors and economies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Pipeline data can identify where representation drops but does not determine whether the appropriate response is recruitment, retention, care support, promotion reform, pay transparency, or broader structural change.

observations.period: 2026; technology, AI roles, and financial-market representation

frontier_scope.value: the report tracks women’s participation in AI-related roles and representation in financial markets

role_distribution.value: women’s participation in the AI economy is growing but concentrated in less technical segments and lower-paid roles

transition_context.value: geoeconomic change, AI, climate, energy, and technological transformation are reshaping jobs, mobility, health, and political pathways

observations.method: WEF synthesis of gender-parity benchmarks with labor-market, corporate, AI, capital-market, and policy-framework analysis.
observations.uncertainty: Emerging AI-role and financial-market indicators may have uneven coverage and evolving occupational definitions; representation does not establish equal pay, influence, or access to capital.
observations.subgroup: Women and men in AI-related work, technical and nontechnical roles, financial markets, leadership, and sectors undergoing digital transition.
observations.counterinterpretation: Growing participation can create new routes to mobility and influence if training, hiring, capital, and governance systems broaden access beyond lower-paid or less technical segments.

related_sources.claim: WEF 2026 infographics summarize global parity, regional timing, AI-economy participation, and economic-rights trends.
World Bank Women, Business and the Law 2026 provides complementary legal-framework, supportive-policy, and enforcement context.

boundary: This record adds a cross-country gender-parity route linking labor-market and political representation, leadership pipelines, AI roles, financial markets, and future-of-work transitions. It is not respondent-level analysis, a firm-level promotion panel, a causal gender-pay study, or evidence that representation alone produces equal power or welfare.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official WEF 2026 report preface, benchmarking chapter, leadership pathway chapter, and publication materials were reviewed; index scores, leadership pipeline, AI-role, financial-market, and transition claims were cross-checked.
